title: Rhythm, clapping on the off-beat and the roots of swing
summary: Wooding contrasts European and black rhythm, ring shouts and spirituals, and says they were doing gospel before it was labelled.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Yes. Well, that's what we played for them. And that's one thing about the stride piano, because it had a strict tempo, you see. Now, the difference between American music and European music -- now you take the French. Their altos hit on the beat, like take the French National De Fil. (sings). Well, now, you see, that doesn't, that was the reason why the white race didn't really get to swing, because you notice, even today, when they applaud, they applaud, when they applaud for you or when they clap, they clap on the beat. We're after the beat, you see. And that was the difference, and that was the reason why we have what we call today, swing, jazz, and they didn't have it. Because it was the way you clap. But we got ours from not having any instruments, so our foot was our bass, and the hands was the alto, and the voice was the center. Because long before they had pianos, you know, we had to make our own singing, like at fish frys and all like that, well we didn't have nothin' but to stomp their feet and clap their
hands and sang, sang the different songs.

Well, now, that's where we get -- when we came over here, well naturally, we came over here with rhythm. 'Cause that's the only thing we had, was rhythm. And then we developed ring shouts, what we called. After the spirituals, we had the secular music, was like ring shouts. Where we all get around and we had a leader and they carried us in the church, even. Like we'd say, like you take the song, "Amazing Grace, How it Sweet Sound", we'd say, this leader would say, "Amazing Grace, how sweet sounds to save a soul like me", and the congregation would all sing, "Amazing Grace", and then he'd sing, "And on we go, beyond the great divide", and they'd sing, "On we go.", you see there's a repetition, you know what I mean. But, he'd lead them and that was our main goal. Because, after all, the Baptists was the, I mean the Methodist was the oldest church, and we had long meter that the Baptists took on later. And they had the, more -- gospel, the gospel wasn't known yet.
So, see, we were doin' gospel all the time, but we wasn't knowin' that -- I mean it hadn't been labeled.
